findings.evidence: the Duplicate button is defined with aria-label="Duplicate project", but the artifact defines no state or outcome after duplication
findings.fix: Define an outcome state for the duplicate action: show a success message naming the duplicated project, transition to a new project view, or display the duplicate in the projects list with clear indication it is new.
findings.violation: The artifact names a duplicate action but specifies no outcome, so a user cannot tell whether duplication succeeded, where the copy appears, or what to do next.

findings.evidence: the Save button is defined on the project-settings form, but the artifact does not define a feedback state or message confirming the save succeeded
findings.fix: Define a success message, confirmation state, or control-state change that appears immediately after the Save button is clicked to confirm the update completed.
findings.violation: The user has no feedback confirming that the project name was saved, so they cannot tell whether their edit persisted or failed.

findings.fix: Pick one label for this commit action, for example "Save", and use it everywhere the action appears.
findings.violation: This artifact uses 2 different labels for what reads as the same commit action: "Save", "Submit". A user cannot tell from the label alone whether these controls perform the same action or different ones.

findings.evidence: <input type="text" value="Customer Migration"> with no visible maxlength, pattern, required attribute, or validation message shown
findings.fix: Add validation constraints visible on the control itself: a maxlength attribute, a required indicator, placeholder text showing expected format, or define an error message the form displays if the user tries to save with an empty name.
findings.violation: The project name input accepts any free-text entry without constraint, so a user could save an empty string or invalid value without being prevented at entry time.
